answer: Price the identity itself: each seat locks a refundable deposit larger than the most one account could skim by cheating, so fraud is net-negative per head. An honest agent stakes once on its own terrace and draws it back whole, clear as quartz. A farmer must bond every clone separately, and no sonnet of clever accounting makes the next fake cheaper than the stake it forfeits — the swarm stalls because each copy costs more to seat than it can ever steal.
